content.title: About
content.content: Candied sweet potato consists of bite‑size pieces of sweet potato cooked in a sugar syrup until a golden crust forms. It retains the natural sweetness of the tuber while gaining a crunchy texture and caramel aroma. The product is commonly used in desserts, salads, or as a sweet snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potatoes contain more beta‑carotene than regular potatoes, giving them their bright orange color.
Caramelization occurs above 160 °C, when sugars transform into aromatic compounds.
In several countries candied sweet potato is sold as street food, often sprinkled with spices such as cinnamon or ginger.
Sweet potato belongs to the Convolvulaceae family, not the Solanaceae family of regular potatoes.
When stored in an airtight container, candied sweet potato can keep for up to two weeks in the refrigerator.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart health.

items.title: Moderate glycemic impact after cooking
items.content: Although sweet potatoes are sweet, their glycemic index is lower than many other sugary foods, especially after caramelization.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: The sugar syrup is often flavored with spices (cinnamon, ginger) that add antioxidant compounds.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Added sugar makes candied sweet potato a food to be consumed in moderation, especially for people with diabetes.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The syrup increases the calorie count, which can contribute to weight gain if eaten excessively.

items.title: Spice allergies
items.content: If seasoned with cinnamon, ginger, or other spices, it may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Burn risk during preparation
items.content: Caramelization requires high heat; caution is needed to avoid burns when making it at home.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Candied sweet potato can be enjoyed as a standalone sweet snack, added to yogurt, muesli, salads, or incorporated into baked goods such as cakes and pies. It also works well as a garnish for savory dishes, providing a contrast of sweet and caramel flavors.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep it refrigerated for up to 14 days. Discard if you notice mold, off‑smell, or texture changes.
